title: Umbra widget manifest (widget.json)
description: Describes one Umbra desktop widget. The same rules are enforced by scripts/catalog.mjs in CI and by the app when it installs a widget.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes (2-40 chars). Must equal the folder name.

name.description: Shown in Settings and the tray menu.

description.description: One sentence for the Browse page.

version.description: Semantic version. Bump it on every change so users see an Update button.

changelog.description: What changed in this version, in a sentence or two. Shown when an update asks the user for new access; the first line is the short form.

entry.description: The page Umbra loads, relative to the widget folder.

preview.description: Screenshot shown in Browse (PNG, 2x, black background).

icon.description: Tab icon for widget groups: a small PNG (64x64 recommended, light grey on transparent, at most 128 px and 64 KB) in the widget folder. Without one the tab shows the first letter of the widget name.

width.description: Logical (96-DPI) pixels; Umbra scales for the display.

themeable.description: Set false to keep the widget's own look: the user's theme is not applied to it.

defaultPosition.description: Offset from the top-left of the primary work area, in logical pixels. Omit to start at the top right.

platforms.description: The operating systems the widget runs on. Leave it out for both. A widget that starts Windows-only programs (powershell, tasklist...) should say ["windows"]: Browse then shows "Windows only" and offers no install on Linux, and a local install there fails with a clear error.

hosts.description: Every HTTPS hostname the widget may contact (fetch, images, scripts, umbra.fetchJson). Everything else is blocked. Hostnames only: no scheme, port or path.

system.description: Read-only machine totals the widget may read with umbra.system(): cpu (load percent), memory (total/used bytes), network (total down/up bytes per second). Numbers only, no process or adapter names. Browse shows these.

notifications.description: Lets the widget call umbra.notify (Windows toast with up to 2 buttons, 5 per 10 minutes). The user must also switch it on for the widget in Settings.

media.description: Windows media session: "read" for umbra.media.nowPlaying (title, artist, album art), "control" for umbra.media.control (play, pause, next, previous; needs a click on the widget).

commands.description: Local programs the widget may start with umbra.run(id, params?). Each is an exact executable plus an argument array (no shell). The user is asked to approve each command the first time it runs, and again whenever it changes. Browse flags widgets that declare commands.

options.description: User settings shown in My widgets, in this order. Values reach the page as umbra.options.<key>.

id.description: What the page passes to umbra.run.

run.description: [executable, ...arguments]. The executable is a plain program name found on PATH ("claude") or an absolute path ("C:\\Tools\\app.exe" on Windows, "/usr/bin/app" on Linux; the other form is simply not found). Each other element is a literal argument, or exactly "${name}" for a declared parameter (never part of a longer string).

description.description: Shown to the user in the approval prompt and in My widgets (not verified by Umbra).

params.description: Named string parameters. Each is passed as one argument, must not start with "-" unless it is one of the fixed choices, and every declared parameter must be supplied.

choices.description: Only these exact values are accepted.

timeoutSeconds.description: The process tree is killed after this long.
